## What the GIL does

CPython's Global Interpreter Lock lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time. Threads still help **I/O-bound** work (they release the GIL while waiting).

## CPU-bound work

Use `multiprocessing` or `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` to use multiple cores, or push hot loops into NumPy/C extensions.

## Free-threading

Python 3.13+ ships an experimental no-GIL build. Know it exists, but don't assume ecosystem/library readiness in production yet.
